protein: Mycobacterium tuberculosis β-lactamase BlaC, wild type
literal_two_peak: cannot tell: Δω and pB of the 860 s-1 process are undetermined; the authors call the four broadened amides 'intermediate to fast'; WT shows no peak doubling (doubling only in G132N and the clavulanate adduct).
reference_state: Wild-type resting-state (free) BlaC, 298 K; pH 6.4, 94 mM sodium MES, 6% D2O, no phosphate

pB: not determined with any accuracy (authors; BLAC-J1, BLAC-r1); the authors' own Bloch-McConnell estimate is that pB must exceed 15% (with Δω > 0.1 ppm 1H and/or 1 ppm 15N at 20 T) if the four broadened amides share the 860 s-1 process (BLAC-J2)
regime: No regime stated for the 860 s-1 process (Δω not determined). For the four anion-site amides broadened beyond detection the authors write that 'an intermediate to fast exchange process may be present in the active site' (2020; BLAC-r1, BLAC-J2).
residues: Group fit: F68, C69, T71, E166, E168, N170, T215, A218 (named in Elings 2021 SI Table S3, doi:10.1128/aac.02628-20; BLAC-J1); broadened beyond detection: Ser70, Ser130, Thr235, Thr237 (Ambler numbering; entry 43, 101, 210, 212 by the project's alignment)
caveats: Whether the four broadened anion-site amides and the 860 s-1 process are one process or two is unresolved. In every BlaC crystal published as of 2020 those four side chains hydrogen-bond a ligand or a buffer anion, and MES (a sulfonate) was never compared with another buffer. Mutant NMR from 2024-2025 used phosphate, which binds the active site, so it is not like-for-like with the WT MES data. A cached SAXS study proposing an open apo shape has no evidence row and was not used.

protein: Human K-Ras4B G-domain (residues 1–169), wild type
literal_two_peak: qualifies: Authors: 'moderately slow', 'intermediate-to-slow' (|Δω|/kex > 0.5); a second CEST dip for state 1 is seen in WT GTP·Mg at 298 K, and 31P γ1/γ2 are separate peaks at 278 K in a C118S background; no HSQC peak doubling for WT at 298 K is reported.

kex: 400 ± 12 s-1 (KRAS-J1, KRAS-r1); 414 ± 3 s-1 (KRAS-J2, KRAS-r26); 404 ± 54 s-1 in PBS/EDTA (KRAS-J3, KRAS-r17)
pB: state 1: 10.15 ± 0.47% (KRAS-r1); 9.6 ± 0.1% (KRAS-r26); 7.8 ± 0.2% higher-energy state (pE) in PBS/EDTA, read as state 1 by the entry (KRAS-r17)

No structure of WT state 1 with native GTP is solved (GDP-like shifts and random-coil-like Switch I only); open-Switch-I crystals exist only for mutants or analogue-bound protein, and state-1 mutants T35S and V29G show extra or faster processes, so state 1 may be heterogeneous.
